title: Repository layout and fixture governance
purpose: Record design-only repository layout proposals for tooling, tests, docs and architecture, and fixtures without moving files or changing command behaviour.

authorityBoundary.notes: This artifact supports Linear discovery closure only. It does not redefine USF semantic authority or approve repository restructuring.

included: tracked and untracked repository files visible from the working tree except pruned heavy directories
top-level and nested directories outside pruned heavy areas
test-like files under tests, compose, and packages/proof/src
scanBoundary.limitation: The scan is layout-oriented. It does not execute tests, validators, proof scripts, or generated reports.

toolingDirectoryLayoutProposal.currentLayout: Tooling is primarily grouped under tools by validator or generator responsibility, with planted-defect fixtures colocated under the owning validator directories. Command entry points are also exposed through package scripts and Make targets.
painPoints: Validator, generator, proof-review, and planted-defect responsibilities are adjacent but not always explicitly typed in the path alone.
Command aliases in Makefile and package scripts can hide the owning tool directory if documentation is not kept synchronized.
Python cache directories and generated-like outputs can distract from source tooling during review.
safeMoves: Do not move tools during discovery closure.
Any future move must preserve compatibility aliases or update all package scripts, Make targets, CI references, docs, fixtures, and planted-defect paths in the same reviewed change.
Shared tool libraries should be introduced only after ownership, import paths, and validator selftests are defined.
Generated outputs must remain separate from source tools and must not become semantic authority.
compatibilityRequirements: Affected package scripts continue to invoke the intended validator or proof command.
Affected Make targets continue to route to current-state aliases or documented compatibility aliases.
Planted-defect fixtures remain resolved by the owning validator.
Documentation references remain accurate after any path move.
No command rename upgrades a readiness claim.

testDirectoryLayoutProposal.currentLayout: Current tests are concentrated under tests by adapters, apps, capabilities, and packages, with proof-related tests also present in packages/proof/src and a generated compose test projection under compose.

futureLocationStrategyByType.strategy: Keep adapter-boundary and provider-substrate tests grouped by adapter responsibility unless a future package split updates imports and command routing.
Keep API, worker, and app contract tests separate from future UI tests until UI readiness gates are explicitly authorised.
Keep semantic capability tests grouped by platform capability and preserve tenant, auth, audit, resource, and provider boundaries.
Use package-level grouping for semantic, integration, resilience, performance, security, supply-chain, and generated-contract tests.
Keep source fixture corpus and its tests together unless a fixture manifest and resolution validator are added.
Treat implementation-adjacent proof tests as proof-package tests and require import-path and command validation before any move.
Retain generated projection separation and source traceability; generated projection does not define authority.

validationExpectations: Future implementation must prove test discovery before and after any move.
Affected command outputs must be unchanged or intentionally updated with documented authority references.
Fixture resolution and planted-defect coverage must remain intact.
Unknown test ownership or missing fixture mapping fails closed to the broader relevant test gate.

docsAdrArchitectureLayoutProposal.currentLayout: Docs currently separate ADRs, architecture documents, assets, and runbooks, while current-state routing and generated or lineage-adjacent guidance live within the architecture document set.

authorityRoleClassification.navigationRule: Surface before lower-authority guidance and never override with agent directives or generated reports.
Keep these as the baseline for semantic and machine-readable governance work.
Treat as normative decisions below semantic definitions and above validators in the USF authority order.
Use as workflow router without overriding Charter, Authority Model, accepted ADRs, validator rules, proof evidence, or semantic instances.
Retain source traceability and lower-authority classification; do not use generated projections to define semantics.

safeNavigationImprovements: Add or maintain reviewer guidance that starts from the current-state authority index and points to constitutional and foundational documents first.
Label generated projections and lineage-adjacent artifacts by authority role before relying on them in future work.
Do not create ADRs or move docs as part of discovery closure.
Any future documentation move must update references and preserve authority order wording.

fixtureClasses.ownershipRule: Owned by the spec validator and schema or instance class under test.
fixtureClasses.validationExpectation: Positive and negative fixture resolution must remain deterministic and fail closed on unknown fixture categories.

fixtureClasses.ownershipRule: Owned by package-level semantic and fixture corpus tests.
fixtureClasses.validationExpectation: Fixture corpus tests must preserve source fixture identity and expected proof semantics.

fixtureClasses.ownershipRule: Owned by compose generation and validation governance, with generated status retained.
fixtureClasses.validationExpectation: Generated fixture/projection output must retain source traceability and must not become semantic authority.

generalLocationRules: Colocate small planted-defect fixtures with the validator that consumes them.
Keep reusable semantic fixture corpora under tests with an explicit manifest or README when reused across commands.
Separate generated fixtures or projections from source fixtures and retain source manifests.

directoryResponsibilityMap.purpose: Map current directory responsibilities for discovery-only optimisation decisions. This map does not move files or redefine semantic authority.

entries.responsibility: semantic, governance, design, current-state routing, and validation-design documents
entries.authorityNote: Authority depends on document class; generated reports and lineage-adjacent documents remain lower authority.
ADRs sit below semantic definitions and above validator rules in the USF authority order.
Registry entries catalogue and resolve artifacts; they do not by themselves activate planned schemas.
Taxonomy values remain distinct from vocabulary values and schemas.
Vocabulary values constrain allowed values and aliases.
Schema files require registry consistency and lifecycle controls before active use.

entries.responsibility: semantic instances grouped by semantic class
entries.authorityNote: Instances must parse as strict JSON and remain consistent with catalogues and registries.

entries.responsibility: validators, generators, proof-review tools, and planted-defect fixture owners
entries.authorityNote: Tools enforce or generate evidence; they do not define platform semantics.
Tests prove expected behaviour but do not define semantics by themselves.

entries.responsibility: Compose source and generated projection artifacts
entries.authorityNote: Generated compose projections are lower authority than semantic definitions and retained source inputs.

entries.responsibility: generated or retained proof and report outputs
entries.authorityNote: Pruned from this layout scan and lower authority than raw evidence and semantic definitions.
Pruned from this layout scan; retained evidence must not be deleted or reclassified by discovery-only work.
Workflow routing must preserve current-state command semantics and non-claims.

schemaLocations.lifecycleRule: Planned schemas remain planned unless the schema file exists, parses as valid JSON Schema, is validator-checkable, and is intentionally promoted under registry and authority rules.
schemaLocations.namingRule: Future schema filenames should end with .schema.json and must remain consistent with the schema authoring standard.

instanceLocations.rule: Semantic instances belong under a class-specific directory and must use strict JSON, controlled vocabulary values where applicable, and taxonomy classifications where applicable.

registryCatalogueLocations.rule: Registry, taxonomy, and vocabulary catalogues remain distinct layers and must not be collapsed into schema or instance files.

examplePolicy: Examples must be clearly classified as examples and must not be treated as active schemas, semantic instances, or proof evidence unless separately governed.
Example-like files must parse as strict JSON when JSON-shaped and must preserve source or authority references if used for validation.
generatedClientPolicy: Generated clients must trace to active or explicitly authorised source contracts and retained generator inputs.
Generated clients do not belong under spec/schemas or spec/instances as authority files.
Generated clients remain projections and cannot activate a planned schema or upgrade readiness claims.

inconsistentNameClasses.authorityOwner: current-state command routing and command-surface governance
inconsistentNameClasses.risk: Compatibility aliases can be mistaken for readiness or completeness claims if not labelled as compatibility entry points.
inconsistentNameClasses.safeImprovement: Keep aliases until replacements are separately authorised and validated; document current preferred aliases beside compatibility aliases.

inconsistentNameClasses.authorityOwner: owning generator and source contract or source manifest
inconsistentNameClasses.risk: Generated names can be read as current authority unless source traceability and lower-authority status are explicit.
inconsistentNameClasses.safeImprovement: Retain generated markers and source references; do not rename generated projections without regenerating or validating references.

inconsistentNameClasses.risk: Forbidden canonical names can imply lineage, temporary state, or redundant local naming if introduced as future canonical names.
inconsistentNameClasses.safeImprovement: No forbidden canonical path segment hits observed in the bounded scan outside allowed explanatory content.

requiredCompatibilityWindows: Keep current-state preferred command aliases and historical compatibility aliases together until a separate validated removal plan exists.
Any rename must include reference checks across docs, package scripts, Make targets, workflows, validators, proofs, and evidence references.
No rename or alias removal may change readiness, provider-mode, environment, or proof-level semantics by implication.

prerequisites: Classify the file authority role and owner before retirement.
Confirm the file is not constitutional authority, active semantic definition, accepted ADR, active validator input, required proof evidence, or required source manifest.
Identify current replacement, retained lineage reason, or explicit non-replacement rationale.
Audit references in docs, package scripts, Make targets, workflows, validators, proofs, evidence, and generated reports.
Record owner approval for any file deletion or relocation.
blockers: References from accepted proof, validator, semantic instance, ADR, or command surface.
Deletion would erase retained evidence or lineage required for auditability.
Validation scope is unknown or not run.
validation: Strict JSON parse for JSON files in scope.
Reference checks before and after any removal.
Affected validators and command aliases must run after any removal.
Evidence references and current-state routing must remain accurate.
Repository integrity and rollback instructions must be recorded.
rollbackStrategy: Prefer no deletion until a separate implementation issue approves removal.
If deletion is approved, keep the exact file list, replacement mapping, validation evidence, and restore instructions with the change record.
Restore immediately if reference checks, validators, or proof commands regress.

supersededFileIndexProposal.authorityLabelRule: Candidate files remain retained evidence, lineage, generated projections, or support material unless higher-authority USF artifacts explicitly classify them as current authority.
supersededFileIndexProposal.retentionRule: Retain candidates until a separate retirement issue proves references, owner approval, validation, and rollback.
supersededFileIndexProposal.riskRule: Indexing must not promote retained or generated files above semantic definitions, ADRs, validators, runtime proof evidence, source implementation, or generated reports in the USF authority order.

duplicateContentAudit.method: Exact SHA-256 grouping of text-like files up to one megabyte outside pruned heavy directories. This does not identify near-duplicates.

duplicateGroups.consolidationRisk: Exact content duplication may still be intentional when files serve different authority roles, validators, fixtures, or generated projection contexts.
duplicateGroups.suggestedNextIssue: Open a targeted consolidation issue only after authority owner, reference usage, and validation scope are confirmed.

duplicateContentAudit.authorityOwnerRule: The highest-authority owner among duplicate paths controls interpretation; generated and report-like copies remain lower authority.
duplicateContentAudit.consolidationRiskRule: Do not consolidate similar files unless semantic role, references, validators, proof evidence, and rollback are all confirmed.
duplicateContentAudit.suggestedNextIssueRule: Create separate consolidation issues per duplicate group family rather than batch-deleting files.
